text: Most important: the consult itself gives two different shock energies. The unstable-SVT node says start 50-100J, while the pre-excited AF node says 100-200J synchronized. The strip quotes both (on the cardiovert tile and the WPW tile) and does not reconcile them. Also, this is a stable/unstable/WPW triage with several time-critical paths; it is kept as one strip (the consult forks at svt-start into stable, unstable and suspected WPW) in the order a clinician meets the nodes, with the unstable tile first because it is the most time-critical. The fork labels at svt-start (Stable — Proceed with Vagal Maneuvers / Unstable — Immediate Cardioversion / Suspected WPW) must equal the option labels but the plate key is limited to 1-2 words, so a faithful fork cannot be written under the label rule; a physician should decide whether to split into stable, unstable and WPW cards. On the one-variant strip, tile conditions carry the stable/unstable/WPW distinction.

The drug store has diltiazem only for 'A-Fib rate control (acute)', not for SVT, so diltiazem is a steps tile and its figure carries a dose. The store entry also lists as contraindications EF 40% or less, decompensated heart failure, second/third-degree AV block without pacemaker, and concurrent IV beta-blocker use, which the consult node does not list; the consult lists sick sinus syndrome and hypotension, which the store also lists.

Diltiazem first bolus: the consult says 15-20mg (0.25 mg/kg) IV over 2 minutes and repeat 20-25mg (0.35 mg/kg); the store says 0.25 mg/kg 'typically 20-25 mg' and a second bolus of 0.35 mg/kg. The mg ranges differ. The per-kg doses on the diltiazem tile are quoted text only: it is a steps tile, so no weight box is shown even though the store has weight calculators for diltiazem (AF rate control entry).

The drug store lists IV amiodarone among AV nodal blockers that are contraindicated in WPW + AF; the consult's WPW + pre-excited AF avoid list does not name amiodarone, and the amiodarone node (offered as the refractory rate-control agent, not on the strip) carries no WPW caution. Reported only; nothing on the strip addresses it.
The avoid line quotes adenosine by name on a steps tile; it is a do-NOT instruction, not a dose. No dose is shown on this tile.
The avoid line quotes diltiazem by name on a steps tile; it is a do-NOT instruction, not a dose. No dose is shown on this tile.

Time-critical content NOT on the strip: sedation before cardioversion (propofol, etomidate, midazolam with fentanyl) and pediatric doses; carotid sinus massage and its contraindications; adenosine technique details and the 3 mg / higher-dose modifiers beyond the one quoted line; reading the adenosine response (abrupt termination vs flutter vs no response); atrial flutter pathway (cardioversion energy, ibutilide, anticoagulation); metoprolol and amiodarone as rate control; diltiazem maintenance infusion, monitoring and the repeat-bolus detail beyond what is quoted; post-cardioversion assessment and the WPW-suspected loop; WPW assessment (orthodromic vs antidromic, where blockers may be used cautiously); ibutilide for WPW AF; disposition, discharge and admission. The consult's critical actions are covered as follows: unstable cardioversion, modified Valsalva, adenosine, WPW AF avoid-list and diltiazem are tiles. Also left off: the consult's full avoid list for WPW AF names verapamil and digoxin as well; the heading line that carries the word AVOID starts with an emoji and cannot be quoted clause-complete, so the strip quotes the consult's own shorter line (adenosine, diltiazem, beta-blockers) instead, which omits verapamil and digoxin. Procainamide for WPW AF is on its own tile; ibutilide is not. Escalation to 360J and the consult's 'consider adenosine between shocks' are partly on the strip (escalation only).

Tile order follows the consult's flow for the stable path (vagal, adenosine, rate control) with the unstable cardioversion tile first because it is time-critical (the consult reaches it from the first node by the Unstable option). It differs from the critical-actions list order, which runs unstable, Valsalva, adenosine, WPW AF, diltiazem.

Adenosine: the store says 12 mg repeat 'if no conversion in 1-2 min' and to repeat once if needed; the consult also lists a maximum of 12mg x 2 and says some sources allow 18mg, while the store only says up to 18 mg may be needed with theophylline/caffeine. The consult's central-line, transplant and carbamazepine/dipyridamole 3 mg reduction matches the store. The pediatric adenosine dose in the consult (0.1 mg/kg then 0.2 mg/kg) is not on the strip; the store's pediatric entries have weight calculators but the adult SVT entry has none, so no weight box is shown.

Procainamide: the consult gives 20-50 mg/min IV, max 17 mg/kg, which agrees with the store's loading line. The store also lists maintenance infusion and stopping criteria (hypotension, QRS widening over 50%) that the consult does not mention; they appear in the drug section of the tile only. The per-kg maximum has no weight calculator in the store.
